title: Yawning Face Emoji 🥱 Meaning: Sleepy or Simply Bored?
description: The 🥱 yawning face emoji means tired, and just as often bored or unimpressed. Learn when it is a goodnight text and when it is a put-down aimed at you.
summary: The 🥱 yawning face covers a wide-open mouth with one hand, eyes shut mid-yawn. Literally it means sleepy or ready for bed. Figuratively it means bored or unimpressed, and in arguments and comment sections it is a dismissive way of saying “this is dull” or “try harder.”
meaning: A yawn has two causes, and the emoji inherits both. The innocent one is fatigue: late-night texts, early alarms, long drives, the afternoon slump after lunch. “Up since five 🥱” needs no decoding. In this role it is softer than 😴, describing someone who is still awake but fading. It often doubles as a polite way to end a chat.

The other cause is boredom, and here 🥱 becomes pointed. Replying to someone's opinion, joke or boast with a lone yawn tells them they are tedious. Sports fans post it at rivals, gamers at weak opponents, and people online at takes they consider predictable. It works as a compact insult because it claims the other person is not even worth getting worked up about.

Added in 2019, it filled a real gap: before then there was no dedicated boredom face, and people used 😴 or 🙄 as stand-ins. It is also used self-mockingly by people describing their own dull routines, and affectionately in goodnight messages between partners. The hand over the mouth gives it a polite, slightly smug air that suits both the sleepy and the sarcastic readings.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Between friends and couples it mostly signals the end of the day. “Going to bed 🥱” is a gentle sign-off. In the morning it means not awake yet. If it arrives as the only response to a long message, however, the sender is saying you bored them, which is rarely a joke without other cues.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: This is where the dismissive use thrives. Comments like “same joke as last year 🥱” or a bare 🥱 under a rival's post mean unimpressed. Fans use it after a predictable win by a dominant team, and critics use it for formulaic movies and albums.

contexts.label: In sports and gaming
contexts.body: It is a taunt. Players send it after an easy victory to suggest the opponent offered no challenge, and fan accounts post it during one-sided games. Athletes have long mimed yawns as trash talk, and the emoji is the text version of that gesture.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Limit it to comments about your own tiredness, such as an early flight or a late night. Using it in a channel about a meeting, presentation or colleague's update tells everyone you found it boring, and that tends to be remembered.

examples.text: Can't keep my eyes open 🥱 night!

examples.meaning: Bored by something long and dull.

examples.text: 🥱 wake me up when you have a new argument
examples.meaning: Dismissing someone's point as tired and unoriginal.
Not fully awake and in need of coffee.
Bragging that a victory took no effort.

examples.text: Movie night idea: I fall asleep in ten minutes 🥱

combos.meaning: Yawning now, asleep shortly; a goodnight signal.
Groggy and waiting for the caffeine to work.
Bored and annoyed, a doubly dismissive reaction.
This is putting the sender to sleep, literally or as a jab.

confusedWith.difference: 😴 is already asleep, with Zs floating above. 🥱 is still awake and yawning. Only the yawn carries the “you're boring me” insult; 😴 used that way is milder and less common.
🤭 also raises a hand to its mouth, but it is smiling behind it: giggling, gasping or covering a slip. 🥱 has its mouth wide open in a yawn and expresses tiredness or boredom.
🙄 shows active irritation or disbelief. 🥱 shows indifference, which can sting more because it implies the subject is not worth any reaction at all.

avoid: Do not reply with it to someone's heartfelt or lengthy message unless you intend to be rude.
Avoid it in work discussions about other people's presentations or ideas.
If someone is venting about a real problem, a yawn reads as contempt even if you only meant you were tired.
design: A yellow face with closed eyes and a wide-open mouth, partly covered by a hand raised in front of it. Vendors differ in how much of the mouth the hand hides and whether teeth or a tongue are visible behind it. The hand stays yellow on every platform, since this emoji has no skin tone options.

faqs.a: Either. With mentions of sleep, mornings or long days, it means tired. As a reaction to what someone said or posted, it means bored or unimpressed. The second use is deliberate and usually a put-down.

It can be. Sending it in response to a person's opinion, story or achievement tells them they are boring. Used about your own sleepiness, it is harmless. Think about what it is replying to before sending.

faqs.q: What does 🥱 mean from a guy or girl?
faqs.a: If it comes late at night, they are sleepy and may be winding the conversation down. If it follows something you said during a debate or banter, they are teasing or dismissing you. It has no romantic meaning.

faqs.q: When was the yawning face emoji added?
faqs.a: It was approved in Unicode 12.0 in 2019. Before that, people relied on the sleeping face or the Zzz symbol to express tiredness, and on the eye-roll for boredom.
